title: Should bands reunite
paragraphs: You can’t cross the same river twice, the popular saying goes. This wisdom reminds us that everything changes - expecting to relive your bygone days of success in the same way is unrealistic. But, apparently, this doesn’t apply to music. Over the last decade or so, for one reason or another, a number of high-profile bands have decided to stop resting on their laurels and have reunited. But why?

Earlier this year, rock band Genesis confirmed that they would be embarking on one more tour. In November 2019, the Pussycat Dolls announced a slew of tour dates for April 2020. In 2018, it was the Spice Girls’ comeback. The list goes on. Many bands have found new success in their resurrected form. American alternative rock band The Pixies originally broke up in 1993 after playing for seven years. After an eleven-year hiatus, the band reunited in 2004 and have not stopped.

In some cases, it’s financial reasons that made them go back on the road. “Touring these days is far more lucrative than it used to be,” according to Kara Weisenstein of online publisher Mic. This is because ticket prices have risen to compensate for the piracy that weakened music sales in the 90s, according to online publisher Bloomberg.

‘People are really into nostalgia right now,’ Lance Bass, member of former band NSYNC told Variety magazine. When The Pixies reformed, their 2004 comeback tour sold out within minutes. Is it possible that those teenage fans of yore have grown into nostalgic adults wistful for their youth? Bass thinks so. ‘I think fans just want to feel that innocence and excitement again,’ he says.

But not everybody thinks that these reunions are a good thing. “There’s something noble in not trying to go after past glories,” says NME writer Leonie Cooper. ‘As much as I love ABBA… the fact they refused to risk putting on a show that might not match the excellence of their heyday is pretty impressive.’ Should bands reunite? Opinion is divided. If things don’t go well, they run the risk of being labelled has-beens and tarnishing their reputation. But if their sound is as good as it ever was and the fans are happy, then who’s going to complain? After all, you can never have too much of a good thing.

vocabulary.entry: bygone /ˈbaɪɡɒn/ adj. 过去的；昔日的
vocabulary.example: We often look back on our bygone childhood with fondness.
vocabulary.translation: 我们常常满怀深情地回首逝去的童年时光。

vocabulary.entry: apply to /əˈplaɪ tuː/ 适用于；应用于
vocabulary.example: This rule does not apply to children under the age of 12.
vocabulary.translation: 这条规定不适用于12岁以下的儿童。

vocabulary.entry: high-profile /ˌhaɪ ˈprəʊfaɪl/ adj. 备受瞩目的；知名度高的
vocabulary.example: The high-profile celebrity attended the charity event last night.
vocabulary.translation: 这位备受瞩目的名人昨晚出席了慈善活动。

vocabulary.entry: rest on one's laurels /rest ɒn wʌnz ˈlɒrəls/ 满足于既得荣誉；不思进取（俗语）
vocabulary.example: After winning the championship, the team refused to rest on their laurels and continued training hard.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得冠军后，这支队伍没有满足于既得荣誉，而是继续刻苦训练。

vocabulary.entry: reunite /ˌriːjuːˈnaɪt/ v. （使）重聚；（使）重组
vocabulary.example: The separated family finally reunited after twenty years.
vocabulary.translation: 这家人失散二十年后终于团聚了。

vocabulary.entry: slew /sluː/ n. 大量；许多
vocabulary.example: The store received a slew of complaints about the poor quality of the product.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店收到了大量关于该产品质量不佳的投诉。

vocabulary.entry: comeback /ˈkʌmbæk/ n. 复出；东山再起
vocabulary.example: The athlete made a successful comeback after his injury.
vocabulary.translation: 这位运动员伤愈后成功复出。

vocabulary.entry: resurrected /ˌrezəˈrektɪd/ adj. 复兴的；重组的
vocabulary.example: The resurrected band gave an amazing performance at the festival.
vocabulary.translation: 这支重组后的乐队在音乐节上献上了精彩的演出。

vocabulary.entry: alternative /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ adj. 另类的；非主流的
vocabulary.example: She likes listening to alternative music that is not very popular.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢听那些不太流行的另类音乐。

vocabulary.entry: hiatus /haɪˈeɪtəs/ n. （活动的）暂停期；休止
vocabulary.example: The magazine will be on hiatus for three months and resume publication in June.
vocabulary.translation: 这本杂志将停刊三个月，于六月份复刊。

vocabulary.entry: lucrative /ˈluːkrətɪv/ adj. 利润丰厚的；赚钱的
vocabulary.example: He started a lucrative business selling handmade crafts online.
vocabulary.translation: 他在网上开了一家卖手工艺品的店，生意很赚钱。

vocabulary.entry: piracy /ˈpaɪrəsi/ n. 盗版行为；海盗行为
vocabulary.example: The government has taken measures to combat software piracy.
vocabulary.translation: 政府已采取措施打击软件盗版行为。

vocabulary.entry: compensate for /ˈkɒmpenseɪt fɔː/ 弥补；补偿
vocabulary.example: The company offered to compensate for the loss caused by the delayed delivery.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司提出赔偿因交货延迟造成的损失。

vocabulary.entry: nostalgia /nɒˈstældʒə/ n. 怀旧之情；乡愁
vocabulary.example: The old movie filled her with nostalgia for her hometown.
vocabulary.translation: 这部老电影让她对故乡充满了怀旧之情。

vocabulary.entry: sell out /sel aʊt/ 售罄；卖光
vocabulary.example: All the tickets for the concert sold out within an hour.
vocabulary.translation: 这场音乐会的门票一小时内就全部售罄了。

vocabulary.entry: yore /jɔː(r)/ n. 往昔；昔日
vocabulary.example: Stories of knights and castles belong to days of yore.
vocabulary.translation: 骑士与城堡的故事都属于往昔岁月。

vocabulary.entry: wistful /ˈwɪstfl/ adj. 惆怅的；渴望的
vocabulary.example: She gave a wistful smile when she talked about her childhood friends.
vocabulary.translation: 她谈起儿时的伙伴时，露出了惆怅的笑容。

vocabulary.entry: innocence /ˈɪnəsns/ n. 纯真；清白
vocabulary.example: The child's eyes were full of innocence and curiosity.
vocabulary.translation: 这个孩子的眼睛里充满了纯真与好奇。

vocabulary.entry: heyday /ˈheɪdeɪ/ n. 全盛时期；鼎盛时期
vocabulary.example: The city was in its heyday during the 1920s and 1930s.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市在20世纪二三十年代迎来了全盛时期。

vocabulary.entry: opinion is divided /əˈpɪnjən ɪz dɪˈvaɪdɪd/ 人们意见不一；众说纷纭
vocabulary.example: Opinion is divided on whether the new policy will be effective.
vocabulary.translation: 关于这项新政策是否会奏效，人们意见不一。

vocabulary.entry: has-been /ˈhæz biːn/ n. 过气人物；昔日红人
vocabulary.example: Some people think the once-famous actor is just a has-been now.
vocabulary.translation: 有些人认为这位曾经红极一时的演员现在不过是个过气明星。

vocabulary.entry: tarnish /ˈtɑːnɪʃ/ v. 损害；玷污（名誉等）
vocabulary.example: The scandal tarnished the politician's reputation completely.
vocabulary.translation: 这起丑闻彻底玷污了这位政客的名誉。

sentences.english: ‘People are really into nostalgia right now,’ Lance Bass, member of former band NSYNC told Variety magazine.

sentences.english: When The Pixies reformed, their 2004 comeback tour sold out within minutes.
sentences.chinese: 小妖精乐队重组后，2004年的回归巡演门票几分钟内便销售一空。

sentences.english: Is it possible that those teenage fans of yore have grown into nostalgic adults wistful for their youth?
sentences.chinese: 难道当年那些十几岁的年轻粉丝，如今都已长成怀念青春、渴望重温旧梦的成年人了吗？

sentences.english: Bass thinks so. ‘I think fans just want to feel that innocence and excitement again,’ he says.
sentences.chinese: 巴斯对此深信不疑，他说：“我觉得粉丝们只是想再次体验那种纯真和激动的感觉。”

sentences.english: But not everybody thinks that these reunions are a good thing.
sentences.chinese: 但并非所有人都认为乐队重组是件好事。

sentences.chinese: 英国音乐杂志《新音乐快递》的撰稿人莱奥妮·库珀表示：“不追逐昔日辉煌，本身就是一种高尚的做法。”

sentences.chinese: “我虽然非常喜欢阿巴合唱团……但他们拒绝冒险举办可能无法重现全盛时期水准的演出，这一点着实令人敬佩。”

sentences.chinese: 如果重组后的表现不尽如人意，乐队就有可能被贴上“过气明星”的标签，声誉也会受损。

sentences.english: But if their sound is as good as it ever was and the fans are happy, then who’s going to complain?
sentences.chinese: 但如果他们的音乐水准依然在线，粉丝们也为之欢欣雀跃，那么又有谁会抱怨呢？

sentences.english: After all, you can never have too much of a good thing.
sentences.chinese: 毕竟，好东西永远不嫌多。
